title: Counting To A Billion

scenes.narration: Counting to one billion, one number every second, would take you nearly thirty-two years.
A million takes about eleven and a half days of nonstop counting.
A billion is a thousand millions: thirty-one point seven years, with no sleep.
Count eight hours a day instead, and it takes about ninety-five years.
Start today, never stop, and you finish around the middle of twenty fifty-eight.
Big numbers take longer to say, so the real time is more. Would you try it?

facts.claim: Counting to one million at one number per second takes about 11.6 days
Counting to one billion at one number per second takes about 31.7 years
facts.derivation: 1,000,000,000 s / 31,557,600 s per year (365.25 days x 86,400 s) = 31.69 years. Equivalently 1,000 x 11.57 days = 11,574 days = 31.69 years

facts.claim: At eight hours a day it takes about 95 years
Starting today (20 October 2026) and counting nonstop finishes around mid 2058
facts.derivation: 20 Oct 2026 + 31.69 years = 20 Oct 2057 + 0.69 yr (about 252 days) = late June 2058

facts.claim: The real time is longer than 31.7 years because large numbers take longer than one second to say
facts.derivation: The 31.7 years assumes exactly one second per number, so it is a minimum. Numbers like 'seven hundred sixty-eight million...' take more than one second to speak.

caption: Counting to one billion takes nearly 32 years, with no sleep. Would you try it?
